title: Reading for pleasure, and whether it is dying

turns.speaker: Zane
turns.text: The survey says a quarter of adults read no books at all last year. Not one.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Books, though. That's a format, not an activity. People read enormous amounts of text all day.

turns.speaker: Aoife
turns.text: Not the same kind of reading, mind you. Sustained attention over three hundred pages is a different skill from scrolling.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Agreed, but the surveys measure the object rather than the skill, and then we panic about the wrong number.

turns.speaker: Zane
turns.text: Audiobooks have grown enormously too, and half the arguments about whether that counts are just snobbery.

turns.speaker: Aoife
turns.text: The comprehension research says it's broadly equivalent for narrative and worse for dense material you'd reread.

turns.speaker: Zane
turns.text: Which matches how people actually use it. Novels on a commute, not a textbook.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: The children's figures are the ones I'd worry about. Enjoyment of reading drops sharply around eleven and keeps falling.

turns.speaker: Aoife
turns.text: Which is exactly when it becomes something you are assessed on.

turns.speaker: Zane
turns.text: That's a strong correlation and a convenient story. Is there anything behind it?

turns.speaker: Aoife
turns.text: Schools that protect free choice reading time do hold enjoyment better. It isn't proof, but it points the same way.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: The simplest intervention is letting them read something you personally consider rubbish.

turns.speaker: Zane
turns.text: Which every librarian has been saying for about forty years.

points: A quarter of adults read no books in a year, though Mira argues books are a format rather than the activity.
Aoife maintains sustained reading is a distinct skill from scrolling, and surveys measure the object rather than the skill.
Audiobook comprehension is broadly equivalent for narrative but weaker for dense material, matching how people use them.
Enjoyment of reading among children falls sharply from about age eleven.
Aoife links this to reading becoming an assessed activity, noting schools protecting free choice reading retain enjoyment better.
Mira's proposed intervention is allowing children to read material adults consider worthless.
